{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122524Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/.claude/skills/security\n\n# Smart Contract Security\n\n## What You Probably Got Wrong\n\n**\"Solidity 0.8+ prevents overflows, so I'm safe.\"** Overflow is one of dozens of attack vectors. The big ones today: reentrancy, oracle manipulation, approval exploits, and decimal mishandling.\n\n**\"I tested it and it works.\"** Working correctly is not the same as being secure. Most exploits call functions in orders or with values the developer never considered.\n\n**\"It's a small contract, it doesn't need an audit.\"** The DAO hack was a simple reentrancy bug. The Euler exploit was a single missing check. Size doesn't correlate with safety.\n\n## Critical Vulnerabilities (With Defensive Code)\n\n### 1. Token Decimals Vary\n\n**USDC has 6 decimals, not 18.** This is the #1 source of \"where did my money go?\" bugs.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — assumes 18 decimals. Transfers 1 TRILLION USDC.\nuint256 oneToken = 1e18;\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — check decimals\nuint256 oneToken = 10 ** IERC20Metadata(token).decimals();\n```\n\nCommon decimals:\n| Token | Decimals |\n|-------|----------|\n| USDC, USDT | 6 |\n| WBTC | 8 |\n| DAI, WETH, most tokens | 18 |\n\n**When doing math across tokens with different decimals, normalize first:**\n```solidity\n// Converting USDC amount to 18-decimal internal accounting\nuint256 normalized = usdcAmount * 1e12; // 6 + 12 = 18 decimals\n```\n\n### 2. No Floating Point in Solidity\n\nSolidity has no `float` or `double`. Division truncates to zero.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — this equals 0\nuint256 fivePercent = 5 / 100;\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — basis points (1 bp = 0.01%)\nuint256 FEE_BPS = 500; // 5% = 500 basis points\nuint256 fee = (amount * FEE_BPS) / 10_000;\n```\n\n**Always multiply before dividing.** Division first = precision loss.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — loses precision\nuint256 result = a / b * c;\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — multiply first\nuint256 result = (a * c) / b;\n```\n\nFor complex math, use fixed-point libraries like `PRBMath` or `ABDKMath64x64`.\n\n### 3. Reentrancy\n\nAn external call can call back into your contract before the first call finishes. If you update state AFTER the external call, the attacker re-enters with stale state.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ VULNERABLE — state updated after external call\nfunction withdraw() external {\n    uint256 bal = balances[msg.sender];\n    (bool success,) = msg.sender.call{value: bal}(\"\"); // ← attacker re-enters here\n    require(success);\n    balances[msg.sender] = 0; // Too late — attacker already withdrew again\n}\n\n// ✅ SAFE — Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern + reentrancy guard\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nfunction withdraw() external nonReentrant {\n    uint256 bal = balances[msg.sender];\n    require(bal > 0, \"Nothing to withdraw\");\n    \n    balances[msg.sender] = 0;  // Effect BEFORE interaction\n    \n    (bool success,) = msg.sender.call{value: bal}(\"\");\n    require(success, \"Transfer failed\");\n}\n```\n\n**The pattern: Checks → Effects → Interactions (CEI)**\n1. **Checks** — validate inputs and conditions\n2. **Effects** — update all state\n3. **Interactions** — external calls last\n\nAlways use OpenZeppelin's `ReentrancyGuard` as a safety net on top of CEI.\n\n### 4. SafeERC20\n\nSome tokens (notably USDT) don't return `bool` on `transfer()` and `approve()`. Standard calls will revert even on success.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — breaks with USDT and other non-standard tokens\ntoken.transfer(to, amount);\ntoken.approve(spender, amount);\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — handles all token implementations\nimport {SafeERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\nusing SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n\ntoken.safeTransfer(to, amount);\ntoken.safeApprove(spender, amount);\n```\n\n**Other token quirks to watch for:**\n- **Fee-on-transfer tokens:** Amount received < amount sent. Always check balance before and after.\n- **Rebasing tokens (stETH):** Balance changes without transfers. Use wrapped versions (wstETH).\n- **Pausable tokens (USDC):** Transfers can revert if the token is paused.\n- **Blocklist tokens (USDC, USDT):** Specific addresses can be blocked from transacting.\n\n### 5. Never Use DEX Spot Prices as Oracles\n\nA flash loan can manipulate any pool's spot price within a single transaction. This has caused hundreds of millions in losses.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ DANGEROUS — manipulable in one transaction\nfunction getPrice() internal view returns (uint256) {\n    (uint112 reserve0, uint112 reserve1,) = uniswapPair.getReserves();\n    return (reserve1 * 1e18) / reserve0; // Spot price — easily manipulated\n}\n\n// ✅ SAFE — Chainlink with staleness + sanity checks\nfunction getPrice() internal view returns (uint256) {\n    (, int256 price,, uint256 updatedAt,) = priceFeed.latestRoundData();\n    require(block.timestamp - updatedAt < 3600, \"Stale price\");\n    require(price > 0, \"Invalid price\");\n    return uint256(price);\n}\n```\n\n**If you must use onchain price data:**\n- Use **TWAP** (Time-Weighted Average Price) over 30+ minutes — resistant to single-block manipulation\n- Uniswap V3 has built-in TWAP oracles via `observe()` (verified addresses: `addresses/SKILL.md`)\n- Still less safe than Chainlink for high-value decisions\n\n### 6. Vault Inflation Attack\n\nThe first depositor in an ERC-4626 vault can manipulate the share price to steal from subsequent depositors.\n\n**The attack:**\n1. Attacker deposits 1 wei → gets 1 share\n2. Attacker donates 1000 tokens directly to the vault (not via deposit)\n3. Now 1 share = 1001 tokens\n4. Victim deposits 1999 tokens → gets `1999 * 1 / 2000 = 0 shares` (rounds down)\n5. Attacker redeems 1 share → gets all 3000 tokens\n\n**The fix — virtual offset:**\n```solidity\nfunction convertToShares(uint256 assets) public view returns (uint256) {\n    return assets.mulDiv(\n        totalSupply() + 1e3,    // Virtual shares\n        totalAssets() + 1        // Virtual assets\n    );\n}\n```\n\nThe virtual offset makes the attack uneconomical — the attacker would need to donate enormous amounts to manipulate the ratio.\n\nOpenZeppelin's ERC4626 implementation includes this mitigation by default since v5.\n\n### 7. Infinite Approvals\n\n**Never use `type(uint256).max` as approval amount.**\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ DANGEROUS — if this contract is exploited, attacker drains your entire balance\ntoken.approve(someContract, type(uint256).max);\n\n// ✅ SAFE — approve only what's needed\ntoken.approve(someContract, exactAmountNeeded);\n\n// ✅ ACCEPTABLE — approve a small multiple for repeated interactions\ntoken.approve(someContract, amountPerTx * 5); // 5 transactions worth\n```\n\nIf a contract with infinite approval gets exploited (proxy upgrade bug, governance attack, undiscovered vulnerability), the attacker can drain every approved token from every user who granted unlimited access.\n\n### 8. Access Control\n\nEvery state-changing function needs explicit access control. \"Who should be able to call this?\" is the first question.\n\n```solidity\nimport {Ownable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable.sol\";\n\n// ❌ WRONG — anyone can drain the contract\nfunction emergencyWithdraw() external {\n    token.transfer(msg.sender, token.balanceOf(address(this)));\n}\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — only owner\nfunction emergencyWithdraw() external onlyOwner {\n    token.transfer(owner(), token.balanceOf(address(this)));\n}\n```\n\nFor complex permissions, use OpenZeppelin's `AccessControl` with role-based separation (ADMIN_ROLE, OPERATOR_ROLE, etc.).\n\n### 9. Input Validation\n\nNever trust inputs. Validate everything.\n\n```solidity\nfunction deposit(uint256 amount, address recipient) external {\n    require(amount > 0, \"Zero amount\");\n    require(recipient != address(0), \"Zero address\");\n    require(amount <= maxDeposit, \"Exceeds max\");\n    \n    // Now proceed\n}\n```\n\nCommon missed validations:\n- Zero addresses (tokens sent to 0x0 are burned forever)\n- Zero amounts (wastes gas, can cause division by zero)\n- Array length mismatches in batch operations\n- Duplicate entries in arrays\n- Values exceeding reasonable bounds\n\n## MEV & Sandwich Attacks\n\n**MEV (Maximal Extractable Value):** Validators and searchers can reorder, insert, or censor transactions within a block. They profit by frontrunning your transaction, backrunning it, or both.\n\n### Sandwich Attacks\n\nThe most common MEV attack on DeFi users:\n\n```\n1. You submit: swap 10 ETH → USDC on Uniswap (slippage 1%)\n2. Attacker sees your tx in the mempool\n3. Attacker frontruns: buys USDC before you → price rises\n4. Your swap executes at a worse price (but within your 1% slippage)\n5. Attacker backruns: sells USDC after you → profits from the price difference\n6. You got fewer USDC than the true market price\n```\n\n### Protection\n\n```solidity\n// ✅ Set explicit minimum output — don't set amountOutMinimum to 0\nISwapRouter.ExactInputSingleParams memory params = ISwapRouter\n    .ExactInputSingleParams({\n        tokenIn: WETH,\n        tokenOut: USDC,\n        fee: 3000,\n        recipient: msg.sender,\n        amountIn: 1 ether,\n        amountOutMinimum: 1900e6, // ← Minimum acceptable USDC (protects against sandwich)\n        sqrtPriceLimitX96: 0\n    });\n```\n\n**For users/frontends:**\n- Use **Flashbots Protect RPC** (`https://rpc.flashbots.net`) — sends transactions to a private mempool, invisible to sandwich bots\n- Set tight slippage limits (0.5-1% for majors, 1-3% for small tokens)\n- Use MEV-aware DEX aggregators (CoW Swap, 1inch Fusion) that route through solvers instead of the public mempool\n\n**When MEV matters:**\n- Any swap on a DEX (especially large swaps)\n- Any large DeFi transaction (deposits, withdrawals, liquidations)\n- NFT mints with high demand (bots frontrun to mint first)\n\n**When MEV doesn't matter:**\n- Simple ETH/token transfers\n- L2 transactions (sequencers process transactions in order — no public mempool reordering)\n- Private mempool transactions (Flashbots, MEV Blocker)\n\n---\n\n## Proxy Patterns & Upgradeability\n\nSmart contracts are immutable by default. Proxies let you upgrade the logic while keeping the same address and state.\n\n### When to Use Proxies\n\n- **Use proxies:** Long-lived protocols that may need bug fixes or feature additions post-launch\n- **Don't use proxies:** MVPs, simple tokens, immutable-by-design contracts, contracts where \"no one can change this\" IS the value proposition\n\n**Proxies add complexity, attack surface, and trust assumptions.** Users must trust that the admin won't upgrade to a malicious implementation. Don't use proxies just because you can.\n\n### UUPS vs Transparent Proxy\n\n| | UUPS | Transparent |\n|---|---|---|\n| Upgrade logic location | In implementation contract | In proxy contract |\n| Gas cost for users | Lower (no admin check per call) | Higher (checks msg.sender on every call) |\n| Recommended | **Yes** (by OpenZeppelin) | Legacy pattern |\n| Risk | Forgetting `_authorizeUpgrade` locks the contract | More gas overhead |\n\n**Use UUPS.** It's cheaper, simpler, and what OpenZeppelin recommends.\n\n### UUPS Implementation\n\n```solidity\n// Implementation contract (the logic)\nimport {UUPSUpgradeable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/proxy/utils/UUPSUpgradeable.sol\";\nimport {Initializable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/proxy/utils/Initializable.sol\";\nimport {OwnableUpgradeable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/access/OwnableUpgradeable.sol\";\n\ncontract MyContractV1 is Initializable, UUPSUpgradeable, OwnableUpgradeable {\n    uint256 public value;\n\n    /// @custom:oz-upgrades-unsafe-allow constructor\n    constructor() {\n        _disableInitializers(); // Prevent implementation from being initialized\n    }\n\n    function initialize(address owner) public initializer {\n        __Ownable_init(owner);\n        __UUPSUpgradeable_init();\n        value = 42;\n    }\n\n    function _authorizeUpgrade(address) internal override onlyOwner {}\n}\n```\n\n### Critical Rules\n\n1. **Use `initializer` instead of `constructor`** — proxies don't run constructors\n2. **Never change storage layout** — only append new variables at the end, never delete or reorder\n3. **Use OpenZeppelin's upgradeable contracts** — `@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable`, not `@openzeppelin/contracts`\n4. **Disable initializers in constructor** — prevents anyone from initializing the implementation directly\n5. **Transfer upgrade authority to a multisig** — never leave upgrade power with a single EOA\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — reordering storage breaks everything\n// V1: uint256 a; uint256 b;\n// V2: uint256 b; uint256 a;  ← Swapped! 'a' now reads 'b's value\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — only append\n// V1: uint256 a; uint256 b;\n// V2: uint256 a; uint256 b; uint256 c;  ← New variable at the end\n```\n\n---\n\n## EIP-712 Signatures & Delegatecall\n\n### EIP-712: Typed Structured Data Signing\n\nEIP-712 lets users sign structured data (not just raw bytes) with domain separation and replay protection. Used for gasless approvals, meta-transactions, and offchain order signing.\n\n**When to use:**\n- **Permit (ERC-2612)** — gasless token approvals (user signs, anyone can submit)\n- **Offchain orders** — sign buy/sell orders offchain, settle onchain (0x, Seaport)\n- **Meta-transactions** — user signs intent, relayer submits and pays gas\n\n```solidity\n// EIP-712 domain separator — prevents replay across contracts and chains\nbytes32 public constant DOMAIN_TYPEHASH = keccak256(\n    \"EIP712Domain(string name,string version,uint256 chainId,address verifyingContract)\"\n);\n\nbytes32 public constant PERMIT_TYPEHASH = keccak256(\n    \"Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)\"\n);\n\nfunction permit(\n    address owner, address spender, uint256 value,\n    uint256 deadline, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s\n) external {\n    require(block.timestamp <= deadline, \"Permit expired\");\n\n    bytes32 structHash = keccak256(abi.encode(\n        PERMIT_TYPEHASH, owner, spender, value, nonces[owner]++, deadline\n    ));\n    bytes32 digest = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(\n        \"\\x19\\x01\", DOMAIN_SEPARATOR(), structHash\n    ));\n\n    address recovered = ecrecover(digest, v, r, s);\n    require(recovered == owner, \"Invalid signature\");\n\n    _approve(owner, spender, value);\n}\n```\n\n**Key properties:**\n- **Domain separator** prevents replaying signatures on different contracts or chains\n- **Nonce** prevents replaying the same signature twice\n- **Deadline** prevents stale signatures from being used later\n- In practice, use OpenZeppelin's `EIP712` and `ERC20Permit` — don't implement from scratch\n\n### Delegatecall\n\n`delegatecall` executes another contract's code in the caller's storage context. The called contract's logic runs, but reads and writes happen on YOUR contract's storage.\n\n**This is extremely dangerous if the target is untrusted.**\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ CRITICAL VULNERABILITY — delegatecall to user-supplied address\nfunction execute(address target, bytes calldata data) external {\n    target.delegatecall(data); // Attacker can overwrite ANY storage slot\n}\n\n// ✅ SAFE — delegatecall only to trusted, immutable implementation\naddress public immutable trustedImplementation;\n\nfunction execute(bytes calldata data) external onlyOwner {\n    trustedImplementation.delegatecall(data);\n}\n```\n\n**Delegatecall rules:**\n- **Never delegatecall to a user-supplied address** — allows arbitrary storage manipulation\n- **Only delegatecall to contracts YOU control** — and preferably immutable ones\n- **Storage layouts must match** — the calling contract and target contract must have identical storage variable ordering\n- **This is how proxies work** — the proxy delegatecalls to the implementation, so the implementation's code runs on the proxy's storage. That's why storage layout matters so much for upgradeable contracts.\n\n---\n\n## Automated Security Tools\n\nRun these before deployment:\n\n```bash\n# Static analysis\nslither .                     # Detects common vulnerabilities\nmythril analyze Contract.sol  # Symbolic execution\n\n# Foundry fuzzing (built-in)\nforge test --fuzz-runs 10000  # Fuzz all test functions with random inputs\n\n# Gas optimization (bonus)\nforge test --gas-report       # Identify expensive functions\n```\n\n**Slither findings to NEVER ignore:**\n- Reentrancy vulnerabilities\n- Unchecked return values\n- Arbitrary `delegatecall` or `selfdestruct`\n- Unprotected state-changing functions\n\n## Further Reading\n\n- **OpenZeppelin Contracts:** https://docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts — audited, battle-tested implementations\n- **SWC Registry:** https://swcregistry.io — comprehensive vulnerability catalog\n- **Rekt News:** https://rekt.news — real exploit post-mortems\n- **SpeedRun Ethereum:** https://speedrunethereum.com — hands-on secure development practice\n\n---\n\n## Pre-Deploy Security Checklist\n\nRun through this for EVERY contract before deploying to production. No exceptions.\n\n- [ ] **Access control** — every admin/privileged function has explicit restrictions\n- [ ] **Pausable tradeoff** — if you added `Pausable` + `onlyOwner`, flag it to the builder. A single key that can freeze all users is a censorship vector. Suggest timelocks or multisig governance.\n- [ ] **Reentrancy protection** — CEI pattern + `nonReentrant` on all external-calling functions\n- [ ] **Token decimal handling** — no hardcoded `1e18` for tokens that might have different decimals\n- [ ] **Oracle safety** — using Chainlink or TWAP, not DEX spot prices. Staleness checks present\n- [ ] **Integer math** — multiply before divide. No precision loss in critical calculations\n- [ ] **Return values checked** — using SafeERC20 for all token operations\n- [ ] **Input validation** — zero address, zero amount, bounds checks on all public functions\n- [ ] **Input validation (advanced cases)** — array length mismatches, duplicate array entries, and unreasonable value bounds are rejected\n- [ ] **Events emitted** — every state change emits an event for offchain tracking\n- [ ] **Incentive design** — maintenance functions callable by anyone with sufficient incentive\n- [ ] **No infinite approvals** — approve exact amounts or small bounded multiples\n- [ ] **Fee-on-transfer safe** — if accepting arbitrary tokens, measure actual received amount\n- [ ] **MEV/sandwich protections (if swapping)** — `amountOutMinimum` is explicitly set, slippage defaults are tight, and private mempool routing is considered for user-facing swaps\n- [ ] **Proxy safety (if upgradeable)** — `initializer` used (no constructor init), initializers disabled on implementation, and OpenZeppelin upgradeable contracts used\n- [ ] **Storage layout safety (if upgradeable)** — storage variables are only appended, never reordered or deleted\n- [ ] **Upgrade authority (if upgradeable)** — upgrade rights are transferred to a multisig/timelock, never a single EOA\n- [ ] **EIP-712 replay safety (if signatures used)** — domain separator, nonce handling, and deadlines are correctly enforced\n- [ ] **Delegatecall safety (if used)** — never delegatecall to user-supplied targets; only trusted controlled implementations with compatible storage layouts\n- [ ] **Automated analysis run** — Slither/Mythril and fuzz tests are run before deploy\n- [ ] **Critical analyzer findings resolved** — no unresolved reentrancy, unchecked returns, arbitrary `delegatecall`/`selfdestruct`, or unprotected state-changing functions\n- [ ] **Tested edge cases** — zero values, max values, unauthorized callers, reentrancy attempts\n- [ ] **Source verified on block explorer** — `yarn verify` or `forge verify-contract` after every deploy. Unverified contracts can't be audited by users and look indistinguishable from scams\n\n---\n\nBefore you finish: send a one-line note via [feedback/SKILL.md](https://ethskills.com/feedback/SKILL.md) — issue or praise.\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"27261f22-1141-4f28-a92c-1d73e910194c","uuid":"96a8ffeb-9369-4054-bcb2-77cb7af11f15","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:25:29.007Z","isSynthetic":true}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012N7ZuuGXBCwtu4A9GydW1G","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\n2\t// OpenZeppelin Contracts (last updated v5.1.0) (token/ERC20/extensions/ERC4626.sol)\n3\t\n4\tpragma solidity ^0.8.20;\n5\t\n6\timport {IERC20, IERC20Metadata, ERC20} from \"../ERC20.sol\";\n7\timport {SafeERC20} from \"../utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\n8\timport {IERC4626} from \"../../../interfaces/IERC4626.sol\";\n9\timport {Math} from \"../../../utils/math/Math.sol\";\n10\t\n11\t/**\n12\t * @dev Implementation of the ERC-4626 \"Tokenized Vault Standard\" as defined in\n13\t * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4626[ERC-4626].\n14\t *\n15\t * This extension allows the minting and burning of \"shares\" (represented using the ERC-20 inheritance) in exchange for\n16\t * underlying \"assets\" through standardized {deposit}, {mint}, {redeem} and {burn} workflows. Depositors get a transferable ERC-20 receipt\n///         (the vault's own shares) representing a pro-rata claim on the underlying.\n///         Yield arrives as plain transfers of the underlying into this contract by a\n///         keeper; it is recognised in fixed cycles and streamed to holders linearly.\n///\n/// @dev Design notes that matter for safety:\n///\n///      1. `totalAssets()` is NOT `asset.balanceOf(this)`. It is internal accounting\n///         (`_storedTotal`) minus the still-locked portion of the current reward cycle.\n///         Tokens that arrive by direct transfer are invisible until {syncRewards} is\n///         called, and {syncRewards} only runs once the previous cycle has ended.\n///         This is what stops (a) yield sniping — deposit right before the keeper's\n///         transfer, withdraw right after — and (b) the ERC-4626 donation/inflation\n///         attack, since a donation can no longer move the share price atomically.\n///\n///      2. Deposits measure the balance actually received, so fee-on-transfer tokens\n///         cannot mint shares against assets the vault never got. {mint} (exact-shares)\n///         cannot honour its contract under a transfer fee and reverts instead.\n///\n///      3. No owner, no pauser, no upgrade path. Vaults are listed permissionlessly for\n///         arbitrary tokens, so there is no privileged key that could freeze or drain\n///         them — and equally no rescue function.\ncontract SaveVault is ERC4626, ERC20Permit, ReentrancyGuard {\n    using Math for uint256;\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n\n    /// @notice Length of a reward vesting cycle. Yield recognised by {syncRewards}\n    ///         is released linearly over this window.\n    /// @dev Protocol constant rather than a per-vault parameter: listing is\n    ///      permissionless, so a configurable value could be griefed by whoever\n    ///      creates the vault first.\n    uint64 public constant REWARDS_CYCLE = 24 hours;\n\n    /// @dev Virtual shares/assets offset (OpenZeppelin inflation-attack mitigation).\n    ///      Defence in depth — the cycle accounting above already prevents the atomic\n    ///      donation attack; this covers residual rounding-based share price games.\n    uint8 private constant DECIMALS_OFFSET = 3;\n\n    /// @dev Reject assets whose decimals would make `decimals()` nonsensical or overflow.\n    uint8 private constant MAX_VAULT_DECIMALS = 36;\n\n    /// @notice Assets recognised by the vault, including the full current reward amount.\n    uint256 private _storedTotal;\n    /// @notice Reward recognised at the last sync, vesting from `_lastSync` to `_rewardsCycleEnd`.\n    uint256 private _lastRewardAmount;\n\n    uint64 private _lastSync;\n    uint64 private _rewardsCycleEnd;\n\n    event RewardsSynced(uint256 rewardAmount, uint256 storedTotal, uint64 cycleEnd);\n    /// @dev Emitted when the vault is empty of shares and residual balance is written off\n    ///      to the next depositor. See {_prepare}.\n    event AccountingReset(uint256 residualBalance);\n\n    error ZeroAmount();\n    error ZeroAddress();\n    error ZeroShares();\n    error NoAssetsReceived();\n    error FeeOnTransferMintUnsupported();\n    error RewardsCycleActive(uint64 cycleEnd);\n    error UnsupportedDecimals();\n\n    constructor(IERC20 asset_, string memory name_, string memory symbol_)\n        ERC4626(asset_)\n        ERC20(name_, symbol_)\n        ERC20Permit(name_)\n    {\n        // Reverts (panic) if the asset reports absurd decimals; explicit error otherwise.\n        if (decimals() > MAX_VAULT_DECIMALS) revert UnsupportedDecimals();\n\n        _lastSync = uint64(block.timestamp);\n        _rewardsCycleEnd = uint64(block.timestamp);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- accounting\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    /// @dev Internal accounting minus the unvested part of the current reward cycle.\n    ///      Deliberately not balance-based; see the contract-level notes.\n    function totalAssets() public view override returns (uint256) {\n        return _storedTotal - lockedRewards();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Portion of the current reward cycle that has not vested yet.\n    function lockedRewards() public view returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 rewardAmount = _lastRewardAmount;\n        uint64 end = _rewardsCycleEnd;\n        if (rewardAmount == 0 || block.timestamp >= end) return 0;\n\n        uint64 start = _lastSync;\n        // `end` is always `start + REWARDS_CYCLE`, so the denominator is non-zero.\n        uint256 vested = rewardAmount.mulDiv(block.timestamp - start, end - start, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n        return rewardAmount - vested;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Assets recognised so far, including rewards still vesting.\n    function storedTotal() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return _storedTotal;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Timestamp at which the current reward cycle finishes vesting.\n    function rewardsCycleEnd() external view returns (uint64) {\n        return _rewardsCycleEnd;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Underlying sitting in the contract that has not been recognised yet.\n    ///         This is what the next {syncRewards} will start vesting.\n    function pendingRewards() public view returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 balance = IERC20(asset()).balanceOf(address(this));\n        uint256 stored = _storedTotal;\n        return balance > stored ? balance - stored : 0;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Recognise underlying that has been transferred in since the last cycle and\n    ///         start streaming it to holders over {REWARDS_CYCLE}.\n    /// @dev Permissionless — anyone may call it, and deposits/withdrawals call it\n    ///      automatically once the cycle has ended, so no dedicated cron is required.\n    ///      It cannot be called mid-cycle: that is what makes yield unsnipeable.\n    function syncRewards() external nonReentrant {\n        if (block.timestamp < _rewardsCycleEnd) revert RewardsCycleActive(_rewardsCycleEnd);\n        _syncRewards();\n    }\n\n    function _syncRewards() private {\n        uint256 balance = IERC20(asset()).balanceOf(address(this));\n        uint256 stored = _storedTotal;\n\n        // A shortfall (negative-rebasing asset, blocklisted vault, token bug) is written\n        // down pro-rata rather than left to be discovered by the last withdrawer.\n        uint256 rewardAmount = balance > stored ? balance - stored : 0;\n\n        _storedTotal = balance;\n        _lastRewardAmount = rewardAmount;\n        _lastSync = uint64(block.timestamp);\n        uint64 end = uint64(block.timestamp) + REWARDS_CYCLE;\n        _rewardsCycleEnd = end;\n\n        emit RewardsSynced(rewardAmount, balance, end);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Run before every deposit/withdrawal so accounting is current.\n    function _prepare() private {\n        if (totalSupply() == 0) {\n            // Nobody holds a claim, so any residual balance (rounding dust, or yield that\n            // landed while the vault was empty) belongs to no one. Zero the accounting so\n            // it cannot skew the next depositor's share price, and let the residual be\n            // picked up as a reward on a later sync.\n            uint256 residual = IERC20(asset()).balanceOf(address(this));\n            if (_storedTotal != 0 || _lastRewardAmount != 0) emit AccountingReset(residual);\n\n            _storedTotal = 0;\n            _lastRewardAmount = 0;\n            _lastSync = uint64(block.timestamp);\n            _rewardsCycleEnd = uint64(block.timestamp);\n            return;\n        }\n\n        if (block.timestamp >= _rewardsCycleEnd) _syncRewards();\n    }\n\n    function _decimalsOffset() internal pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return DECIMALS_OFFSET;\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------- deposit\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    /// @dev Shares are minted against the balance actually received, so a fee-on-transfer\n    ///      asset dilutes only the depositor making the deposit, never existing holders.\n    ///      `previewDeposit` cannot know the token's fee, so it may overstate the result\n    ///      for such assets — integrators should check the return value.\n    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 shares)\n    {\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        _prepare();\n\n        // Snapshot before the pull: `_convertToShares` must price the deposit against the\n        // vault as it stood before these assets arrived.\n        uint256 assetsBefore = totalAssets();\n        uint256 received = _pullAsset(msg.sender, assets);\n\n        shares = received.mulDiv(totalSupply() + 10 ** DECIMALS_OFFSET, assetsBefore + 1, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n\n        _storedTotal += received;\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, received, shares);\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    /// @dev Reverts for fee-on-transfer assets: `mint` promises an exact share count for a\n    ///      quoted asset amount, which cannot hold when the vault receives less than it pulls.\n    ///      Use {deposit} instead.\n    function mint(uint256 shares, address receiver)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 assets)\n    {\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        _prepare();\n\n        assets = previewMint(shares);\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        uint256 received = _pullAsset(msg.sender, assets);\n        if (received < assets) revert FeeOnTransferMintUnsupported();\n\n        _storedTotal += received;\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, received, shares);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Pull `amount` from `from` and return what actually landed.\n    function _pullAsset(address from, uint256 amount) private returns (uint256 received) {\n        IERC20 token = IERC20(asset());\n        uint256 balanceBefore = token.balanceOf(address(this));\n        token.safeTransferFrom(from, address(this), amount);\n        uint256 balanceAfter = token.balanceOf(address(this));\n\n        if (balanceAfter <= balanceBefore) revert NoAssetsReceived();\n        received = balanceAfter - balanceBefore;\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ withdraw\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    function withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256)\n    {\n        _prepare();\n        return super.withdraw(assets, receiver, owner);\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    function redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256)\n    {\n        _prepare();\n        return super.redeem(shares, receiver, owner);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Burns before transferring (checks-effects-interactions), inherited from ERC4626.\n    function _withdraw(address caller, address receiver, address owner, uint256 assets, uint256 shares)\n        internal\n        override\n    {\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n        if (assets == 0 || shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        // Invariant: `assets <= totalAssets() <= _storedTotal`, so this cannot underflow.\n        // Kept as a checked subtraction anyway — it is the last line of defence if the\n        // conversion math is ever wrong.\n        _storedTotal -= assets;\n\n        super._withdraw(caller, receiver, owner, assets, shares);\n    }\n\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------- ERC-20\n\n    function decimals() public view override(ERC4626, ERC20) returns (uint8) {\n        return super.decimals();\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5506,"cache_read_input_tokens":41488,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5506},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"27261f22-1141-4f28-a92c-1d73e910194c","uuid":"399daea6-3fcc-4e52-9487-1ca0e5188437","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:31:18.814Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTLo5mC5SfUFcgQttv2"}

_syncRewards();\n    }\n\n    function _decimalsOffset() internal pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return DECIMALS_OFFSET;\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------- deposit\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    /// @dev Shares are minted against the balance actually received, so a fee-on-transfer\n    ///      asset dilutes only the depositor making the deposit, never existing holders.\n    ///      `previewDeposit` cannot know the token's fee, so it may overstate the result\n    ///      for such assets — integrators should check the return value.\n    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256 shares)\n    {\n        if (assets == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n\n        _prepare();\n\n        // Snapshot before the pull: `_convertToShares` must price the deposit against the\n        // vault as it stood before these assets arrived.\n        uint256 assetsBefore = totalAssets();\n        uint256 received = _pullAsset(msg.sender, assets);\n\n        shares = received.mulDiv(totalSupply() + 10 ** DECIMALS_OFFSET, assetsBefore + 1, Math.Rounding.Floor);\n        if (shares == 0) revert ZeroShares();\n\n        _storedTotal += received;\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n\n        emit Deposit(msg.sender, receiver, received, shares);\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    /// @dev Reverts for }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ withdraw\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    function withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)\n  function redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner)\n        public\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n        returns (uint256)\n    {\n        _prepare();\n        return {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTbeJqZQKDS7VRw79bT","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Etxxu8mn22QdX11WmLVa3f","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122524Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/src/SaveVaultFactory.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {IERC20Metadata} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/IERC20Metadata.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nimport {SaveVault} from \"./SaveVault.sol\";\n\n/// @title SaveVaultFactory\n/// @notice Permissionless registry: anyone can list any ERC-20 and get exactly one\n///         {SaveVault} for it. The factory has no owner and no privileged functions —\n///         listing something here is not an endorsement of the token.\n/// @dev Vaults are deployed with CREATE2 salted by the asset address, so a vault's\n///      address is derivable offchain from the asset alone.\ncontract SaveVaultFactory is ReentrancyGuard {\n    /// @notice asset => vault. `address(0)` means not listed.\n    mapping(address asset => address vault) public vaultFor;\n\n    /// @notice Every vault ever created, in creation order.\n    address[] public allVaults;\n\n    event VaultCreated(address indexed asset, address indexed vault, uint256 index);\n\n    error ZeroAddress();\n    error AssetNotAContract(address asset);\n    error AssetNotERC20(address asset);\n    error VaultAlreadyExists(address asset, address vault);\n    error OnlySelf();\n\n    /// @notice Deploy the vault for `asset`.\n    /// @dev `nonReentrant` because the vault constructor calls into `asset` (decimals),\n    ///      and metadata probing calls into it twice more — an adversarial token must not\n    ///      be able to re-enter and race the registry write.\n    function createVault(address asset) external nonReentrant returns (address vault) {\n        if (asset == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n        if (asset.code.length == 0) revert AssetNotAContract(asset);\n\n        address existing = vaultFor[asset];\n        if (existing != address(0)) revert VaultAlreadyExists(asset, existing);\n\n        // Minimum viable ERC-20 surface. Anything that cannot answer `balanceOf` is not\n        // a token this vault can account for.\n        (bool ok, bytes memory data) =\n            asset.staticcall(abi.encodeCall(IERC20.balanceOf, (address(this))));\n        if (!ok || data.length < 32) revert AssetNotERC20(asset);\n\n        (string memory name, string memory symbol) = _vaultMetadata(asset);\n\n        vault = address(\n            new SaveVault{salt: bytes32(uint256(uint160(asset)))}(IERC20(asset), name, symbol)\n        );\n\n        vaultFor[asset] = vault;\n        allVaults.push(vault);\n\n        emit VaultCreated(asset, vault, allVaults.length - 1);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Number of vaults created so far.\n    function vaultCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return allVaults.length;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Address the vault for `asset` will have (or already has).\n    function predictVaultAddress(address asset) external view returns (address) {\n        (string memory name, string memory symbol) = _vaultMetadata(asset);\n        bytes32 initCodeHash = keccak256(\n            abi.encodePacked(type(SaveVault).creationCode, abi.encode(IERC20(asset), name, symbol))\n        );\n        return address(\n            uint160(\n                uint256(\n                    keccak256(\n                        abi.encodePacked(\n                            bytes1(0xff), address(this), bytes32(uint256(uint160(asset))), initCodeHash\n                        )\n                    )\n                )\n            )\n        );\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ metadata\n\n    function _vaultMetadata(address asset)\n        private\n        view\n        returns (string memory name, string memory symbol)\n    {\n        string memory assetName = _readString(asset, IERC20Metadata.name.selector);\n        string memory assetSymbol = _readString(asset, IERC20Metadata.symbol.selector);\n\n        name = string.concat(\"Save \", bytes(assetName).length == 0 ? \"Token\" : assetName);\n        symbol = string.concat(\"sv\", bytes(assetSymbol).length == 0 ? \"TOKEN\" : assetSymbol);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev `name()`/`symbol()` are optional and, on real tokens, inconsistently typed\n    ///      (MKR returns `bytes32`) or missing entirely. Decoding attacker-controlled\n    ///      return data can revert, so the decode happens behind an external self-call\n    ///      that `try/catch` can contain.\n    function _readString(address token, bytes4 selector) private view returns (string memory) {\n        try SaveVaultFactory(address(this)).decodeStringReturn(token, selector) returns (\n            string memory value\n        ) {\n            return value;\n        } catch {\n            return \"\";\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @dev External only so it can be `try`-ed. Not meant to be called directly.\n    function decodeStringReturn(address token, bytes4 selector)\n        external\n        view\n        returns (string memory)\n    {\n        if (msg.sender != address(this)) revert OnlySelf();\n\n        (bool ok, bytes memory data) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(selector));\n        if (!ok || data.length == 0) return \"\";\n\n        // bytes32-style metadata (MKR and other pre-standard tokens).\n        if (data.length == 32) return _fromBytes32(abi.decode(data, (bytes32)));\n\n        // May revert on malformed return data; the caller catches it.\n        string memory value = abi.decode(data, (string));\n        return _truncate(value, 32);\n    }\n\n    function _fromBytes32(bytes32 raw) private pure returns (string memory) {\n        uint256 length;\n        while (length < 32 && raw[length] != 0) length++;\n\n        bytes memory buffer = new bytes(length);\n        for (uint256 i; i < length; ++i) buffer[i] = raw[i];\n        return string(buffer);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Caps how much attacker-chosen text ends up in the vault's own name/symbol.\n    function _truncate(string memory value, uint256 maxLength) private pure returns (string memory) {\n        bytes memory raw = bytes(value);\n        if (raw.length <= maxLength) return value;\n\n        bytes memory buffer = new bytes(maxLength);\n        for (uint256 i; i < maxLength; ++i) buffer[i] = raw[i];\n        return string(buffer);\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":17375,"cache_read_input_tokens":46994,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":17375},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"27261f22-1141-4f28-a92c-1d73e910194c","uuid":"10d26670-a882-4137-8b2d-a4dfe97ea063","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:31:44.848Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTbaqEQC5MPLgCVSChx"}

 }\n\n    function symbol() external pure returns (string memory) {\n        revert(\"no symbol\");\n    }\n}\n\n/// @dev Returns garbage that `abi.decode(..., (string))` cannot parse.\ncontract ABI head for a string.\n        return hex\"ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff\";\n    }\n}\n\ninterface IVaultLike {\n    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver) external returns (uint256);\n    function syncRewards() external;\n}\n\n/// @dev ERC-777-style: calls back into the vault during `transferFrom`.\ncontract ReentrantToken is ERC20 {\n    IVaultLike public vault;\n    bool public attacking;\n\n    constructor() ERC20(\"Reentrant\", \"RE\") {}\n\n    function setVault(address vault_) external {\n        vault = IVaultLike(vault_);\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n\n    function arm() external {\n        attacking = true;\n    }\n\n    function _update(address from, address to, uint256 value) internal override {\n        super._update(from, to, value);\n        if (attacking && from != address(0) && to == address(vault)) {\n            attacking = false;\n }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":402,"cache_read_input_tokens":66920,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":402},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"27261f22-1141-4f28-a92c-1d73e910194c","uuid":"37ff783b-3246-42d0-92fb-1ef15c641b37","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:32:17.435Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTdtnHpDCriAUtcG4TN"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTfvz43qxPcwaC8yHwk","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_014ATWm73CqfhfvAAvw4xv4X","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122524Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/test/SaveVault.t.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nimport {SaveVault} from \"../src/SaveVault.sol\";\nimport {SaveVaultFactory} from \"../src/SaveVaultFactory.sol\";\nimport {MockERC20, FeeOnTransferToken, ReentrantToken} from \"./mocks/Tokens.sol\";\n\ncontract SaveVaultTest is Test {\n    SaveVaultFactory factory;\n    MockERC20 usdc; // 6 decimals, to keep decimal handling honest\n    SaveVault vault;\n\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n\n    uint256 constant ONE = 1e6;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        factory = new SaveVaultFactory();\n        usdc = new MockERC20(\"USD Coin\", \"USDC\", 6);\n        vault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(usdc)));\n\n        usdc.mint(alice, 1_000_000 * ONE);\n        usdc.mint(bob, 1_000_000 * ONE);\n        usdc.mint(keeper, 1_000_000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    function _deposit(address who, uint256 amount) internal returns (uint256) {\n        vm.prank(who);\n        return vault.deposit(amount, who);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------- basics\n\n    function test_metadataFollowsUnderlying() public view {\n        assertEq(vault.name(), \"Save USD Coin\");\n        assertEq(vault.symbol(), \"svUSDC\");\n        // 6 (underlying) + 3 (virtual offset)\n        assertEq(vault.decimals(), 9);\n        assertEq(vault.asset(), address(usdc));\n    }\n\n    function test_depositThenRedeemRoundTrip() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        assertGt(shares, 0);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n\n        assertEq(assets, 1000 * ONE);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n    }\n\n    function test_claimIsProRata() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _deposit(bob, 3000 * ONE);\n\n        // Keeper yield, recognised and fully vested.\n        _harvest(400 * ONE);\n\n        // 1:3 split of 400.\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1100 * ONE, 2);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 3300 * ONE, 2);\n    }\n\n    function test_receiptTokenIsTransferable() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.transfer(bob, shares);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, bob, bob);\n        assertEq(assets, 1000 * ONE);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- yield vesting\n\n    /// Keeper sends tokens; they stay invisible until a cycle boundary, then stream.\n    function test_yieldIsInvisibleUntilSyncThenVestsLinearly() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n\n        // Mid-cycle: nothing recognised, and sync is not allowed.\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000 * ONE);\n        assertEq(vault.pendingRewards(), 100 * ONE);\n        vm.expectRevert(\n            abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVault.RewardsCycleActive.selector, vault.rewardsCycleEnd())\n        );\n        vault.syncRewards();\n\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n        vault.syncRewards();\n\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000 * ONE, \"locked at sync\");\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 12 hours);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.totalAssets(), 1050 * ONE, 1, \"half vested\");\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 12 hours);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1100 * ONE, \"fully vested\");\n    }\n\n    /// The attack this vault is shaped around: deposit just before the keeper's transfer,\n    /// withdraw just after, and walk away with yield you were never at risk for.\n    function test_yieldSnipingIsUnprofitable() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        uint256 bobBefore = usdc.balanceOf(bob);\n\n        // Bob front-runs the keeper.\n        uint256 bobShares = _deposit(bob, 1000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n\n        // ...and back-runs it in the same block.\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.redeem(bobShares, bob, bob);\n\n        assertLe(usdc.balanceOf(bob), bobBefore, \"sniper must not profit\");\n\n        // The yield is still there for Alice, who actually held through the cycle.\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n        vault.syncRewards();\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + vault.REWARDS_CYCLE());\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1100 * ONE, 2);\n    }\n\n    /// Even waiting out the cycle only earns a sniper the vested slice they were present for.\n    function test_snipingAfterSyncOnlyEarnsVestedSlice() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n        vault.syncRewards();\n\n        uint256 bobBefore = usdc.balanceOf(bob);\n        uint256 bobShares = _deposit(bob, 1000 * ONE);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.redeem(bobShares, bob, bob);\n\n        assertLe(usdc.balanceOf(bob), bobBefore, \"no instant profit right after sync\");\n    }\n\n    function test_syncRewardsIsPermissionless() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n\n        vm.prank(makeAddr(\"randomBot\"));\n        vault.syncRewards();\n        assertEq(vault.pendingRewards(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// Deposits pick up a finished cycle on their own, so no cron is strictly required.\n    function test_depositAutoSyncsAfterCycleEnd() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n\n        _deposit(bob, 1 * ONE);\n        assertEq(vault.pendingRewards(), 0, \"deposit synced the cycle\");\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------- inflation attack\n\n    function test_inflationAttackDoesNotZeroOutVictim() public {\n        // Attacker seeds the empty vault with 1 wei...\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(1, bob);\n\n        // ...and donates to inflate the share price.\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100_000 * ONE);\n\n        // Donation is not recognised, so the price did not move at all.\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1);\n\n        uint256 victimShares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        assertGt(victimShares, 0, \"victim must not be rounded to zero shares\");\n\n        // Attacker cannot walk off with the victim's deposit.\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 attackerTake = vault.redeem(vault.balanceOf(bob), bob, bob);\n        assertLt(attackerTake, 1000 * ONE);\n    }\n\n    function test_depositRevertsIfItWouldMintZeroShares() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        // No path here mints zero for a sane amount; guard exists for extreme ratios.\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.deposit(0, bob);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------- fee-on-transfer\n\n    function test_feeOnTransferDepositCreditsOnlyWhatArrived() public {\n        FeeOnTransferToken fee = new FeeOnTransferToken(500); // 5%\n        SaveVault feeVault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(fee)));\n\n        fee.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        feeVault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // 950 arrived; the vault must account for 950, not 1000.\n        assertEq(feeVault.totalAssets(), 950e18);\n        assertEq(fee.balanceOf(address(feeVault)), 950e18);\n    }\n\n    /// A second depositor must not be diluted by the first one's transfer fee.\n    function test_feeOnTransferDoesNotDiluteExistingHolders() public {\n        FeeOnTransferToken fee = new FeeOnTransferToken(500);\n        SaveVault feeVault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(fee)));\n\n        fee.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        fee.mint(bob, 1000e18);\n\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        feeVault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        uint256 aliceClaimBefore = feeVault.maxWithdraw(alice);\n\n        vm.startPrank(bob);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        feeVault.deposit(1000e18, bob);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        assertApproxEqAbs(feeVault.maxWithdraw(alice), aliceClaimBefore, 1);\n    }\n\n    function test_mintRevertsForFeeOnTransferAsset() public {\n        FeeOnTransferToken fee = new FeeOnTransferToken(500);\n        SaveVault feeVault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(fee)));\n\n        fee.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.FeeOnTransferMintUnsupported.selector);\n        feeVault.mint(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_mintWorksForWellBehavedAsset() public {\n        uint256 shares = 1000 * 10 ** vault.decimals();\n        uint256 quoted = vault.previewMint(shares);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 spent = vault.mint(shares, alice);\n\n        assertEq(spent, quoted);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------- reentrancy & inputs\n\n    function test_reentrantAssetCannotReenterDeposit() public {\n        ReentrantToken evil = new ReentrantToken();\n        SaveVault evilVault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(evil)));\n        evil.setVault(address(evilVault));\n\n        evil.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        evil.approve(address(evilVault), type(uint256).max);\n        evil.arm();\n        vm.expectRevert(ReentrancyGuard.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.selector);\n        evilVault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_rejectsZeroAddressReceiver() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        vault.deposit(100 * ONE, address(0));\n\n        _deposit(alice, 100 * ONE);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        vault.withdraw(1 * ONE, address(0), alice);\n    }\n\n    function test_cannotWithdrawSomeoneElsesShares() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.redeem(shares, bob, alice);\n    }\n\n    function test_withdrawWithAllowance() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.approve(bob, shares);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.redeem(shares, bob, alice);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(bob), 1_000_000 * ONE + 1000 * ONE);\n    }\n\n    /// Emptying the vault must not leave accounting that bricks the next depositor.\n    function test_vaultRecoversAfterBeingEmptied() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        assertEq(vault.totalSupply(), 0);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 500 * ONE); // stranded yield, no holders\n\n        uint256 bobShares = _deposit(bob, 1000 * ONE);\n        assertGt(bobShares, 0);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000 * ONE, \"stranded balance not counted as bob's\");\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------- fuzzing\n\n    function testFuzz_depositRedeemNeverExceedsDeposit(uint256 amount) public {\n        amount = bound(amount, 1e3, 1_000_000 * ONE);\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, amount);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        assertLe(out, amount, \"must not extract more than deposited\");\n    }\n\n    function testFuzz_secondDepositorCannotDiluteFirst(uint256 first, uint256 second) public {\n        first = bound(first, 1e3, 500_000 * ONE);\n        second = bound(second, 1e3, 500_000 * ONE);\n\n        _deposit(alice, first);\n        uint256 aliceClaim = vault.maxWithdraw(alice);\n        _deposit(bob, second);\n\n        assertGe(vault.maxWithdraw(alice) + 2, aliceClaim, \"alice's claim must not shrink\");\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------- helpers\n\n    /// Move past the initial cycle so tests start from a clean boundary.\n    function _startFreshCycle() internal {\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + vault.REWARDS_CYCLE() + 1);\n        vault.syncRewards();\n    }\n\n    /// Keeper transfer, recognised and fully vested.\n    function _harvest(uint256 amount) internal {\n        _startFreshCycle();\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), amount);\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n        vault.syncRewards();\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + vault.REWARDS_CYCLE());\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2458,"cache_read_input_tokens":67322,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2458},"output_tokens":50,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"27261f22-1141-4f28-a92c-1d73e910194c","uuid":"39a531f5-ab3d-4678-a14a-f1e465e61462","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:33:14.919Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTfuiQDMFrFLxm9tFGk"}

SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nimport {SaveVault} from \"../src/SaveVault.sol\";\nimport {SaveVaultFactory} from \"../src/SaveVaultFactory.sol\";\nimport {MockERC20, FeeOnTransferToken, ReentrantToken} from \"./mocks/Tokens.sol\";\n\ncontract SaveVaultTest is Test {\n    SaveVaultFactory factory;\n    MockERC20 usdc; // 6 decimals, to keep decimal handling honest\n    SaveVault vault;\n\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n\n    uint256 constant ONE = 1e6;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        factory = new SaveVaultFactory();\n        usdc = new MockERC20(\"USD Coin\", \"USDC\", 6);\n        vault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(usdc)));\n\n        usdc.mint(alice, 1_000_000 * ONE);\n        usdc.mint(bob, 1_000_000 * ONE);\n        usdc.mint(keeper, 1_000_000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    function _deposit(address who, uint256 amount) internal returns (uint256) {\n        vm.prank(who);\n        return vault.deposit(amount, who);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------- basics\n\n    function test_metadataFollowsUnderlying() public view {\n        assertEq(vault.name(), \"Save USD Coin\");\n        assertEq(vault.symbol(), \"svUSDC\");\n        // 6 (underlying) + 3 (virtual offset)\n        assertEq(vault.decimals(), 9);\n        assertEq(vault.asset(), address(usdc));\n    }\n\n    function test_depositThenRedeemRoundTrip() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        assertGt(shares, 0);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n\n        assertEq(assets, 1000 * ONE);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n    }\n\n    function test_claimIsProRata() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _deposit(bob, 3000 * ONE);\n\n        // Keeper yield, recognised and fully vested.\n        _harvest(400 * ONE);\n\n        // 1:3 split of 400.\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1100 * ONE, 2);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 3300 * ONE, 2);\n    }\n\n    function test_receiptTokenIsTransferable() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.transfer(bob, shares);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, bob, bob);\n        assertEq(assets, 1000 * ONE);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- yield vesting\n\n    /// Keeper sends tokens; they stay invisible until a cycle boundary, then stream.\n    function test_yieldIsInvisibleUntilSyncThenVestsLinearly() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n\n        // Mid-cycle: nothing recognised, and sync is not allowed.\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000 * ONE);\n        assertEq(vault.pendingRewards(), 100 * ONE);\n        vm.expectRevert(\n            abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVault.RewardsCycleActive.selector, vault.rewardsCycleEnd())\n        );\n        vault.syncRewards();\n\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n        vault.syncRewards();\n\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000 * ONE, \"locked at sync\");\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 12 hours);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.totalAssets(), 1050 * ONE, 1, \"half vested\");\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 12 hours);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1100 * ONE, \"fully vested\");\n    }\n\n    /// The attack this vault is shaped around: deposit just before the keeper's transfer,\n    /// withdraw just after, and walk away with yield you were never at risk for.\n    function test_yieldSnipingIsUnprofitable() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        uint256 bobBefore = usdc.balanceOf(bob);\n\n        // Bob front-runs the keeper.\n        uint256 bobShares = _deposit(bob, 1000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n\n        // ...and back-runs it in the same block.\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.redeem(bobShares, bob, bob);\n\n        assertLe(usdc.balanceOf(bob), bobBefore, \"sniper must not profit\");\n\n        // The yield is still there for Alice, who actually held through the cycle.\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n        vault.syncRewards();\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + vault.REWARDS_CYCLE());\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1100 * ONE, 2);\n    }\n\n    /// Even waiting out the cycle only earns a sniper the vested slice they were present for.\n    function test_snipingAfterSyncOnlyEarnsVestedSlice() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n        vault.syncRewards();\n\n        uint256 bobBefore = usdc.balanceOf(bob);\n        uint256 bobShares = _deposit(bob, 1000 * ONE);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.redeem(bobShares, bob, bob);\n\n        assertLe(usdc.balanceOf(bob), bobBefore, \"no instant profit right after sync\");\n    }\n\n    function test_syncRewardsIsPermissionless() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n\n        vm.prank(makeAddr(\"randomBot\"));\n        vault.syncRewards();\n        assertEq(vault.pendingRewards(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// Deposits pick up a finished cycle on their own, so no cron is strictly required.\n    function test_depositAutoSyncsAfterCycleEnd() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n\n        _deposit(bob, 1 * ONE);\n        assertEq(vault.pendingRewards(), 0, \"deposit synced the cycle\");\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------- inflation attack\n\n    function test_inflationAttackDoesNotZeroOutVictim() public {\n        // Attacker seeds the empty vault with 1 wei...\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(1, bob);\n\n        // ...and donates to inflate the share price.\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100_000 * ONE);\n\n        // Donation is not recognised, so the price did not move at all.\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1);\n\n        uint256 victimShares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        assertGt(victimShares, 0, \"victim must not be rounded to zero shares\");\n\n        // Attacker cannot walk off with the victim's deposit.\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 attackerTake = vault.redeem(vault.balanceOf(bob), bob, bob);\n        assertLt(attackerTake, 1000 * ONE);\n    }\n\n    function test_depositRevertsIfItWouldMintZeroShares() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        // No path here mints zero for a sane amount; guard exists for extreme ratios.\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.deposit(0, bob);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------- fee-on-transfer\n\n    function test_feeOnTransferDepositCreditsOnlyWhatArrived() public {\n        FeeOnTransferToken fee = new FeeOnTransferToken(500); // 5%\n        SaveVault feeVault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(fee)));\n\n        fee.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        feeVault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // 950 arrived; the vault must account for 950, not 1000.\n        assertEq(feeVault.totalAssets(), 950e18);\n        assertEq(fee.balanceOf(address(feeVault)), 950e18);\n    }\n\n    /// A second depositor must not be diluted by the first one's transfer fee.\n    function test_feeOnTransferDoesNotDiluteExistingHolders() public {\n        FeeOnTransferToken fee = new FeeOnTransferToken(500);\n        SaveVault feeVault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(fee)));\n\n        fee.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        fee.mint(bob, 1000e18);\n\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        feeVault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        uint256 aliceClaimBefore = feeVault.maxWithdraw(alice);\n\n        vm.startPrank(bob);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        feeVault.deposit(1000e18, bob);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        assertApproxEqAbs(feeVault.maxWithdraw(alice), aliceClaimBefore, 1);\n    }\n\n    function test_mintRevertsForFeeOnTransferAsset() public {\n        FeeOnTransferToken fee = new FeeOnTransferToken(500);\n        SaveVault feeVault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(fee)));\n\n        fee.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.FeeOnTransferMintUnsupported.selector);\n        feeVault.mint(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_mintWorksForWellBehavedAsset() public {\n        uint256 shares = 1000 * 10 ** vault.decimals();\n        uint256 quoted = vault.previewMint(shares);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 spent = vault.mint(shares, alice);\n\n        assertEq(spent, quoted);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------- reentrancy & inputs\n\n    function test_reentrantAssetCannotReenterDeposit() public {\n        ReentrantToken evil = new ReentrantToken();\n        SaveVault evilVault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(evil)));\n        evil.setVault(address(evilVault));\n\n        evil.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        evil.approve(address(evilVault), type(uint256).max);\n        evil.arm();\n        vm.expectRevert(ReentrancyGuard.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.selector);\n        evilVault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_rejectsZeroAddressReceiver() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        vault.deposit(100 * ONE, address(0));\n\n        _deposit(alice, 100 * ONE);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        vault.withdraw(1 * ONE, address(0), alice);\n    }\n\n    function test_cannotWithdrawSomeoneElsesShares() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.redeem(shares, bob, alice);\n    }\n\n    function test_withdrawWithAllowance() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.approve(bob, shares);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.redeem(shares, bob, alice);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(bob), 1_000_000 * ONE + 1000 * ONE);\n    }\n\n    /// Emptying the vault must not leave accounting that bricks the next depositor.\n    function test_vaultRecoversAfterBeingEmptied() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        assertEq(vault.totalSupply(), 0);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 500 * ONE); // stranded yield, no holders\n\n        uint256 bobShares = _deposit(bob, 1000 * ONE);\n        assertGt(bobShares, 0);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000 * ONE, \"stranded balance not counted as bob's\");\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------- fuzzing\n\n    function testFuzz_depositRedeemNeverExceedsDeposit(uint256 amount) public {\n        amount = bound(amount, 1e3, 1_000_000 * ONE);\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, amount);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        assertLe(out, amount, \"must not extract more than deposited\");\n    }\n\n    function testFuzz_secondDepositorCannotDiluteFirst(uint256 first, uint256 second) public {\n        first = bound(first, 1e3, 500_000 * ONE);\n        second = bound(second, 1e3, 500_000 * ONE);\n\n        _deposit(alice, first);\n        uint256 aliceClaim = vault.maxWithdraw(alice);\n        _deposit(bob, second);\n\n        assertGe(vault.maxWithdraw(alice) + 2, aliceClaim, \"alice's claim must not shrink\");\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------- helpers\n\n    /// Move past the initial cycle so tests start from a clean boundary.\n    function _startFreshCycle() internal {\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + vault.REWARDS_CYCLE() + 1);\n        vault.syncRewards();\n    }\n\n    /// Keeper transfer, recognised and fully vested.\n    function _harvest(uint256 amount) internal {\n        _startFreshCycle();\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), amount);\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n        vault.syncRewards();\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + vault.REWARDS_CYCLE());\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}
