_deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        vm.prank(bob);","originalFile":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nimport {SaveVault} from \"../src/SaveVault.sol\";\nimport {SaveVaultFactory} from \"../src/SaveVaultFactory.sol\";\nimport {MockERC20, FeeOnTransferToken, ReentrantToken} from \"./mocks/Tokens.sol\";\n\ncontract SaveVaultTest is Test {\n    SaveVaultFactory factory;\n    MockERC20 usdc; // 6 decimals, to keep decimal handling honest\n    SaveVault vault;\n\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n\n    uint256 constant ONE = 1e6;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        factory = new SaveVaultFactory();\n        usdc = new MockERC20(\"USD Coin\", \"USDC\", 6);\n        vault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(usdc)));\n\n        usdc.mint(alice, 1_000_000 * ONE);\n        usdc.mint(bob, 1_000_000 * ONE);\n        usdc.mint(keeper, 1_000_000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    function _deposit(address who, uint256 amount) internal returns (uint256) {\n        vm.prank(who);\n        return vault.deposit(amount, who);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------- basics\n\n    function test_metadataFollowsUnderlying() public view {\n        assertEq(vault.name(), \"Save USD Coin\");\n        assertEq(vault.symbol(), \"svUSDC\");\n        // 6 (underlying) + 3 (virtual offset)\n        assertEq(vault.decimals(), 9);\n        assertEq(vault.asset(), address(usdc));\n    }\n\n    function test_depositThenRedeemRoundTrip() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        assertGt(shares, 0);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n\n        assertEq(assets, 1000 * ONE);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n    }\n\n    function test_claimIsProRata() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _deposit(bob, 3000 * ONE);\n\n        // Keeper yield, recognised and fully vested.\n        _harvest(400 * ONE);\n\n        // 1:3 split of 400.\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1100 * ONE, 2);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(bob), 3300 * ONE, 2);\n    }\n\n    function test_receiptTokenIsTransferable() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.transfer(bob, shares);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 assets = vault.redeem(shares, bob, bob);\n        assertEq(assets, 1000 * ONE);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- yield vesting\n\n    /// Keeper sends tokens; they stay invisible until a cycle boundary, then stream.\n    function test_yieldIsInvisibleUntilSyncThenVestsLinearly() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n\n        // Mid-cycle: nothing recognised, and sync is not allowed.\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000 * ONE);\n        assertEq(vault.pendingRewards(), 100 * ONE);\n        vm.expectRevert(\n            abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVault.RewardsCycleActive.selector, vault.rewardsCycleEnd())\n        );\n        vault.syncRewards();\n\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n        vault.syncRewards();\n\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1000 * ONE, \"locked at sync\");\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 12 hours);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.totalAssets(), 1050 * ONE, 1, \"half vested\");\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 12 hours);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1100 * ONE, \"fully vested\");\n    }\n\n    /// The attack this vault is shaped around: deposit just before the keeper's transfer,\n    /// withdraw just after, and walk away with yield you were never at risk for.\n    function test_yieldSnipingIsUnprofitable() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        uint256 bobBefore = usdc.balanceOf(bob);\n\n        // Bob front-runs the keeper.\n        uint256 bobShares = _deposit(bob, 1000 * ONE);\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n\n        // ...and back-runs it in the same block.\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.redeem(bobShares, bob, bob);\n\n        assertLe(usdc.balanceOf(bob), bobBefore, \"sniper must not profit\");\n\n        // The yield is still there for Alice, who actually held through the cycle.\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n        vault.syncRewards();\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + vault.REWARDS_CYCLE());\n        assertApproxEqAbs(vault.maxWithdraw(alice), 1100 * ONE, 2);\n    }\n\n    /// Even waiting out the cycle only earns a sniper the vested slice they were present for.\n    function test_snipingAfterSyncOnlyEarnsVestedSlice() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n        vault.syncRewards();\n\n        uint256 bobBefore = usdc.balanceOf(bob);\n        uint256 bobShares = _deposit(bob, 1000 * ONE);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.redeem(bobShares, bob, bob);\n\n        assertLe(usdc.balanceOf(bob), bobBefore, \"no instant profit right after sync\");\n    }\n\n    function test_syncRewardsIsPermissionless() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n\n        vm.prank(makeAddr(\"randomBot\"));\n        vault.syncRewards();\n        assertEq(vault.pendingRewards(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// Deposits pick up a finished cycle on their own, so no cron is strictly required.\n    function test_depositAutoSyncsAfterCycleEnd() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        _startFreshCycle();\n\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100 * ONE);\n        vm.warp(vault.rewardsCycleEnd());\n\n        _deposit(bob, 1 * ONE);\n        assertEq(vault.pendingRewards(), 0, \"deposit synced the cycle\");\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------- inflation attack\n\n    function test_inflationAttackDoesNotZeroOutVictim() public {\n        // Attacker seeds the empty vault with 1 wei...\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(1, bob);\n\n        // ...and donates to inflate the share price.\n        vm.prank(keeper);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 100_000 * ONE);\n\n        // Donation is not recognised, so the price did not move at all.\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1);\n\n        uint256 victimShares = _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        assertGt(victimShares, 0, \"victim must not be rounded to zero shares\");\n\n        // Attacker cannot walk off with the victim's deposit.\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 attackerTake = vault.redeem(vault.balanceOf(bob), bob, bob);\n        assertLt(attackerTake, 1000 * ONE);\n    }\n\n    function test_depositRevertsIfItWouldMintZeroShares() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1000 * ONE);\n        // No path here mints zero for a sane amount; guard exists for extreme ratios.\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.deposit(0, bob);\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------- fee-on-transfer\n\n    function test_feeOnTransferDepositCreditsOnlyWhatArrived() public {\n        FeeOnTransferToken fee = new FeeOnTransferToken(500); // 5%\n        SaveVault feeVault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(fee)));\n\n        fee.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        feeVault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // 950 arrived; the vault must account for 950, not 1000.\n        assertEq(feeVault.totalAssets(), 950e18);\n        assertEq(fee.balanceOf(address(feeVault)), 950e18);\n    }\n\n    /// A second depositor must not be diluted by the first one's transfer fee.\n    function test_feeOnTransferDoesNotDiluteExistingHolders() public {\n        FeeOnTransferToken fee = new FeeOnTransferToken(500);\n        SaveVault feeVault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(fee)));\n\n        fee.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        fee.mint(bob, 1000e18);\n\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        feeVault.deposit(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        uint256 aliceClaimBefore = feeVault.maxWithdraw(alice);\n\n        vm.startPrank(bob);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        feeVault.deposit(1000e18, bob);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        assertApproxEqAbs(feeVault.maxWithdraw(alice), aliceClaimBefore, 1);\n    }\n\n    function test_mintRevertsForFeeOnTransferAsset() public {\n        FeeOnTransferToken fee = new FeeOnTransferToken(500);\n        SaveVault feeVault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(fee)));\n\n        fee.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.FeeOnTransferMintUnsupported.selector);\n        feeVault.mint(1000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_mintWorksForWellBehavedAsset() public {\n        uint256 shares = 1000 * 10 ** vault.decimals();\n        uint256 quoted = vault.previewMint(shares);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 spent = vault.mint(shares, alice);\n\n        assertEq(spent, quoted);\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), shares);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------- reentrancy & inputs\n\n    function test_reentrantAssetCannotReenterDeposit() public {\n        ReentrantToken evil = new ReentrantToken();\n        SaveVault evilVault = SaveVault(factory.createVault(address(evil)));\n        evil.setVault(address(evilVault));\n\n        evil.mint(alice, 1000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        evil.approve(address(evilVault), type(uint256).max);\n        evil.arm();\n        vm.expectRevert(ReentrancyGuard.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.selector);\n        evilVault.deposit(100e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_rejectsZeroAddressReceiver() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        vault.deposit(100 * ONE, address(0));\n\n        _deposit(alice, 100 * ONE);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        vault.withdraw(1 * ONE, address(0), alice);\n    }\n\n    function test_cannotWithdrawSomeoneElsesShares() public {\n        uint256 shares = assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(bob), 1_000_000 * ONE + 1000 * ONE);\n    }\n\n    /// Emptying the vault must not leave accounting that bricks the next depositor.\n    function {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTpFV1bkakLzYQxNmS8","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_013Cb9NjVWzuCir6tE4KWcJn","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122524Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/NOTES.md","content":"# Save Vaults — operator notes\n\nTwo contracts:\n\n- `src/SaveVaultFactory.sol` — permissionless registry. `createVault(asset)` deploys exactly\n  one vault per ERC-20, CREATE2-salted by the asset address. No owner, no allowlist.\n- `src/SaveVault.sol` — the vault. ERC-4626, so the receipt is a normal transferable ERC-20\n  (plus ERC-2612 `permit`). No owner, no pause, no upgrade path, no rescue function.\n\n```\nforge build\nforge test\nFOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci forge test   # 10k fuzz runs\n```\n\n---\n\n## How a depositor's claim is computed\n\nThe receipt token is the vault's ERC-4626 share. A holder's claim is their share of\n`totalAssets()`:\n\n```\nshares_minted = assets_received * (totalSupply + 10^3) / (totalAssets + 1)   # rounded down\nassets_owed   = shares          * (totalAssets + 1) / (totalSupply + 10^3)   # rounded down\n```\n\nThree things in that formula are deliberate.\n\n**`assets_received`, not `assets` requested.** `deposit()` measures the vault's balance\nbefore and after the pull and mints against the delta. On a fee-on-transfer token the\ndepositor is credited for what actually landed; existing holders are not diluted by\nsomeone else's transfer tax. Because `previewDeposit()` cannot know a token's fee, it can\noverstate the result for such tokens — integrators should use the value `deposit()`\nreturns, not the preview.\n\n`mint()` (exact shares out) reverts with `FeeOnTransferMintUnsupported` on those tokens: it\npromises an exact share count for a quoted asset amount, and that promise cannot hold when\nthe vault receives less than it pulls. Use `deposit()`.\n\n**The `+10^3` / `+1` virtual offset.** OpenZeppelin's inflation-attack mitigation. It also\nsets the initial exchange rate, which is why the receipt token has 3 more decimals than the\nunderlying (`svUSDC` has 9, `svDAI` has 21). Assets whose `decimals()` would push the vault\npast 36 are rejected at deploy; assets whose `decimals()` reverts default to 18.\n\n**`totalAssets()` is internal accounting, not `asset.balanceOf(vault)`.** This is the main\ndeparture from a stock ERC-4626 and it drives the next section.\n\nRounding is always in the vault's favour, so the pool never owes more than it holds. A\nround trip returns at most what went in — dust stays behind, and is picked up as yield.\n\n## How yield gets recognised\n\nThe keeper just transfers the underlying in. Those tokens are **invisible to the share\nprice until a cycle boundary**, then released linearly:\n\n```\nREWARDS_CYCLE = 24 hours\n\nsyncRewards()   # permissionless; reverts while a cycle is still running\n  reward   = balanceOf(vault) - storedTotal     # everything that arrived since last sync\n  vests linearly from now to now + 24h\n\ntotalAssets() = storedTotal - (unvested part of the current reward)\n```\n\n`deposit`/`mint`/`withdraw`/`redeem` call `syncRewards()` themselves once the cycle has\nended, so no dedicated cron is required — a dedicated caller just makes recognition prompt.\n\n### Why, and what it buys\n\nWith instant deposits, instant withdrawals, no lockup, and yield arriving as a lump\ntransfer, the naive balance-based vault has a free-money bug: watch the mempool for the\nkeeper's transfer, deposit in front of it, withdraw behind it, and collect a slice of yield\nyou were never at risk for. Everyone who actually held through the period pays for it.\n\nDeferring recognition to a cycle boundary and then vesting over 24 hours removes the\natomic profit — a sniper would have to hold across the whole vesting window, which is just\nbeing a depositor. `test_yieldSnipingIsUnprofitable` and\n`test_snipingAfterSyncOnlyEarnsVestedSlice` pin this down.\n\nThe same property kills the ERC-4626 donation/inflation attack outright: the attacker's\ndonation cannot move the share price in the same transaction, or in the same cycle\n(`test_inflationAttackDoesNotZeroOutVictim`). The virtual offset is belt-and-braces on top.\n\nCosts, stated plainly:\n\n- Yield sent mid-cycle sits idle until the cycle ends. Worst case, ~24h of latency.\n- Someone who deposits and leaves inside one cycle earns nothing.\n- Anyone can send tokens to the vault and they become everyone's yield. That is exactly\n  how the keeper works, so it cannot be distinguished or blocked.\n\n`24 hours` is a hard constant rather than a per-vault parameter on purpose. Listing is\npermissionless, so a configurable cycle would let whoever lists a token first pick a hostile\nvalue (e.g. 30 days) and there is no admin to fix it.\n\n---\n\n## What an operator has to get right\n\n### Listing a token\n\n1. **Listing is not endorsement.** `createVault` will happily deploy a vault for a scam\n   token, a rebasing token, or a token whose owner can mint infinitely. The contract cannot\n   judge this. Whatever surfaces the vault list — the frontend — is where curation has to\n   live, or users will assume listed means vetted.\n\n2. **Check the token against the classes below before surfacing it.** The vault survives\n   all of them without corrupting other vaults (each vault holds exactly one asset, so blast\n   radius is contained), but depositors can still lose:\n\n   | Token behaviour | What happens |\n   |---|---|\n   | Fee-on-transfer | Handled. Deposits credit what arrived; `mint()` reverts. Withdrawals also lose the fee, so a round trip returns less than deposited — surface this. |\n   | Rebasing up (stETH) | Positive rebases are indistinguishable from keeper yield and get streamed as such. Works, but prefer the wrapped version (wstETH). |\n   | Rebasing down | Written down pro-rata at the next `syncRewards()`. No stale-price window, but holders take the loss. |\n   | Blocklist (USDC, USDT) | If the *vault* is blocklisted, every withdrawal reverts. There is no admin rescue. Unavoidable for any non-custodial vault; flag it for centrally-controlled assets. |\n   | Pausable | Deposits and withdrawals revert while the token is paused. |\n   | Upgradeable / mintable by owner | Token owner can mint themselves the whole pool's worth. Nothing onchain can prevent this. |\n   | Missing/odd metadata | Handled. `bytes32` name/symbol (MKR) decoded, reverting or malformed metadata falls back to `Save Token` / `svTOKEN`, missing `decimals()` defaults to 18. |\n   | ERC-777 / callback hooks | Reentrancy is blocked (`nonReentrant` + checks-effects-interactions). |\n   | > 36 decimals | Rejected at deploy. |\n\n3. **Seed the vault.** Not required for safety — the cycle accounting already blocks the\n   inflation attack — but a non-trivial first deposit keeps the share price sane and avoids\n   confusing rounding for the first few small depositors.\n\n4. **Verify the vault on the explorer** right after `createVault`. Vaults are deployed by\n   the factory, so they will not auto-verify:\n   ```\n   forge verify-contract <vault> src/SaveVault.sol:SaveVault \\\n     --constructor-args $(cast abi-encode \"constructor(address,string,string)\" <asset> \"<name>\" \"<symbol>\")\n   ```\n\n### Running the keeper\n\n1. **Cadence should be at least the cycle length (24h).** Sending more often is safe but\n   pointless: transfers that arrive mid-cycle just queue up in `pendingRewards()` and get\n   recognised in one lump at the next boundary. Sending *less* often than 24h is fine too —\n   the vault simply idles.\n\n2. **Never send yield to a vault with zero shares.** It belongs to no one, and the next\n   depositor picks it up as a windfall. The vault's accounting resets itself when supply\n   hits zero so this cannot brick deposits (`test_vaultRecoversAfterBeingEmptied`), but the\n   tokens are gone from your budget. Check `totalSupply() > 0` before transferring.\n\n3. **Use a private mempool (Flashbots Protect / MEV Blocker) for the keeper transfer\n   anyway.** The vesting design means a visible transfer is no longer profitable to\n   sandwich, so this is defence in depth rather than the primary control — but it costs\n   nothing.\n\n4. **Call `syncRewards()` after the cycle ends** if you want yield recognised promptly.\n   It is permissionless and idempotent-ish (reverts with `RewardsCycleActive` if called\n   early). Skipping it is not dangerous — the next deposit or withdrawal does it — but\n   yield sits unrecognised until someone interacts.\n\n5. **`send tokens ≠ approve`.** The vault never pulls from the keeper. Do not grant it an\n   allowance; there is no code path that would use one.\n\n6. **Monitor `pendingRewards()` and `RewardsSynced` events.** A growing `pendingRewards()`\n   with no `RewardsSynced` means nobody is interacting with the vault and yield is stalled.\n\n### Accepted trade-offs\n\n- **No admin key at all.** No pause, no upgrade, no rescue. For permissionless listing of\n  arbitrary tokens this is the right call — a pause key over every vault is a censorship\n  vector and a single point of failure, and an upgrade key over vaults holding other\n  people's money is worse. The cost is that nothing can be fixed after deploy and tokens\n  sent to a vault by mistake (including foreign ERC-20s) are unrecoverable. If a bug is\n  found, the response is to deploy a new factory and migrate.\n- **Non-underlying tokens sent to a vault are stuck.** Deliberate: a sweep function on an\n  ownerless contract is a footgun, and giving it an owner reintroduces the admin key.\n- **One vault per token, first-come.** Whoever lists first sets nothing configurable, so\n  there is nothing to grief — but a token can never be re-listed with different parameters.\n\n### Before deploying\n\nDone here:\n- CEI + `nonReentrant` on every asset-moving path, incl. adversarial-token reentrancy test\n- `SafeERC20` throughout (USDT-style non-returning tokens)\n- No hardcoded `1e18`; decimals read from the asset with a safe fallback\n- Multiply-before-divide via `Math.mulDiv`; rounding always favours the pool\n- Zero-address / zero-amount / zero-share validation on every entrypoint\n- Events on every state change (`Deposit`, `Withdraw`, `RewardsSynced`, `AccountingReset`,\n  `VaultCreated`)\n- No oracles, no swaps, no delegatecall, no proxies, no approvals granted by the vault\n- 30 tests incl. fuzz at 10k runs\n\nStill outstanding:\n- **Run Slither and Mythril.** Not installed in this environment, so this has not been\n  done: `slither .` and `mythril analyze src/SaveVault.sol`.\n- **External audit** before mainnet. A holder's claim is their share of\n`totalAssets()`:\n\n```\nshares_minted = assets_received * (totalSupply + 10^3) / (totalAssets + 1)   # rounded down\nassets_owed   = shares          * (totalAssets + 1) / (totalSupply + 10^3)   # rounded down\n```\n\nThree things in that formula are deliberate.\n\n**`assets_received`, not `assets` requested.** `deposit()` measures the vault's balance\nbefore and after the pull and mints against the delta. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTu7yTbn7ADqsBaHo1E","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"`forge build` clean, 30 tests pass (fuzz at 10k runs).\n\n## What's there\n\n- `src/SaveVaultFactory.sol` — permissionless registry, one CREATE2 vault per ERC-20, no owner.\n- `src/SaveVault.sol` — ERC-4626 vault; shares are the transferable receipt (plus ERC-2612 `permit`). No owner, pause, upgrade, or rescue.\n- `test/` — 30 tests incl. reentrancy, fee-on-transfer, inflation attack, odd metadata, fuzz.\n- `NOTES.md`, `script/Deploy.s.sol`.\n\n## One design call worth your pushback\n\nI took \"the keeper just sends tokens in\" as given, but changed how the vault *receives* it. `totalAssets()` is internal accounting, not `asset.balanceOf(vault)`: transfers in are invisible until a cycle boundary, then vest linearly over 24h.\n\nReason: instant deposits + instant withdrawals + lump-sum yield is a free-money bug. Deposit in front of the keeper's transfer, withdraw behind it, take a cut of yield you never held risk for. Balance-based accounting can't distinguish that from a real depositor. The same property blocks the ERC-4626 donation/inflation attack outright, since a donation can no longer move the share price atomically.\n\nCosts, in `NOTES.md` too: yield sent mid-cycle idles up to ~24h, and deposit-and-leave-within-a-cycle earns nothing. The 24h cycle is a hard constant, not a per-vault param — permissionless listing means a configurable value could be griefed by whoever lists first, with no admin to fix it.\n\nIf you'd rather have plain balance-based accounting and handle sniping off-chain (private mempool + small frequent drips), that's a much smaller contract — say the word.\n\n## Other notable decisions\n\n- `deposit()` mints against measured balance delta, so fee-on-transfer tokens dilute only the depositor. `mint()` reverts for them — it can't honor exact-shares-for-quoted-assets.\n- Receipt decimals = underlying + 3 (virtual offset). `svUSDC` is 9 decimals, `svDAI` is 21.\n- Zero admin key anywhere.
